title_en: Jiao Jianjun v. Jiangsu Zhongshan International Travel Service Co., Ltd. and China Kanghui Nanjing International Travel Service Co., Ltd. (Third Party) — dispute over tourism infringement
ruling_gist_en: After a tourist enters into a tourism contract with a travel agency, the two parties form a tourism service contract relationship. The travel agency must provide services that meet the requirements of ensuring the personal safety and property security of the tourist. Meanwhile, the food, accommodation, transportation and other services provided by the tourism auxiliary service provider entrusted by the travel agency are a continuation of the travel agency's performance of its obligations under the tourism service contract and shall be deemed as acts on behalf of the travel agency. The tortious acts of the tourism auxiliary service provider may be directly deemed as tortious acts of the travel agency. If a tourist suffers personal injury or property damage due to a traffic accident while riding a vehicle provided by the travel agency during the tour, this constitutes a concurrence of liability for breach of contract and tort liability. The tourist has the right to choose either a contractual action or a tort action to claim corresponding civil compensation liability from the travel agency.

full_text_en:
Jiao Jianjun v. Jiangsu Zhongshan International Travel Service Co., Ltd. and Third Party China Comfort Nanjing International Travel Service Co., Ltd. — Dispute over Tourism Tort

【Ruling Summary】

After a tourist enters into a tourism contract with a travel agency, a tourism service contract relationship is formed between the two parties, and the services provided by the travel agency shall meet the requirements of ensuring the personal safety and property security of the tourist. Meanwhile, the accommodation, transportation, and other services provided by the tourism auxiliary entrusted by the travel agency are a continuation of the travel agency's performance of its obligations under the tourism service contract and shall be deemed as acts on behalf of the travel agency; the tortious acts of the tourism auxiliary may be directly deemed as the tortious acts of the travel agency. Where a tourist suffers personal injury or property damage due to a traffic accident while taking a vehicle provided by the travel agency during the tour, this constitutes a concurrence of liability for breach of contract and tort liability, and the tourist has the right to choose either a contractual claim or a tort claim to demand that the travel agency bear corresponding civil damages.

Where a travel agency unilaterally transfers its tourism business to another travel agency without authorization, the travel agency that signed the tourism contract and the travel agency that actually provides the tourism services shall bear joint and several liability.

Plaintiff: Jiao Jianjun, female, 59 years old, Han ethnicity, employee of Nanjing Xiaoyushan Culture Communication Co., Ltd., residing at Luolang Lane, Baixia District, Nanjing.

Defendant: Jiangsu Zhongshan International Travel Service Co., Ltd., domiciled at Hanzhong Road, Gulou District, Nanjing.
Legal Representative: Yang Xun, General Manager of the Company.

Third Party: China Comfort Nanjing International Travel Service Co., Ltd., domiciled at New Model Road, Gulou District, Nanjing.
Legal Representative: Li Jilie, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun filed a lawsuit with the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing against Defendant Jiangsu Zhongshan International Travel Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongshan International Travel Service) and Third Party China Comfort Nanjing International Travel Service Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Comfort Travel Service) regarding a tourism tort dispute.

Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun alleged: On December 15, 2008, the plaintiff participated in an 11-day tour to Thailand, Singapore, and Malaysia organized by the defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service, paid the defendant a group fee of RMB 6,560, and signed the "Jiangsu Province Outbound Tourism Contract." On the evening of December 26, 2008, the plaintiff and other domestic tourists were taking a tourist bus arranged by the defendant from a scenic spot back to Bangkok when a serious traffic accident occurred, causing the plaintiff's spleen rupture, closed fracture of the left clavicle, fracture of seven left ribs, hemothorax, and compression fracture of the lumbar spine. The plaintiff was immediately sent to a Thai hospital for emergency treatment and hospitalization. During this period, the plaintiff was shuttled back and forth by the Thai side and the defendant, with no one caring for her. Not only did the plaintiff fail to receive compensation and consolation money from the Thai side for each injured person, but she returned to China with her injured and ill body. It was not until several months later that the plaintiff learned that her group had been transferred to the third party Comfort Travel Service, and this irresponsible subcontracting of tourists by the defendant was done without the plaintiff's consent. Because the Thai travel agency had purchased travel accident insurance for each tourist in accordance with relevant Thai laws, the defendant and the third party should have stepped forward to claim compensation for the plaintiff. The defendant and the third party violated this obligation and should first pay the plaintiff the RMB 60,000 that should have been compensated by Thailand. After returning to China, the plaintiff was admitted to Jiangsu Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine on February 27, 2009, for continued treatment. A second surgery was performed to remove the shoulder plate, and the required costs should be paid by the defendant and the third party. The defendant should also compensate the plaintiff for personal accident insurance benefits. In the concurrence of liability for breach of contract and tort, the plaintiff chooses a tort claim and requests the court to: 1. Order the defendant and the third party to jointly and severally compensate the plaintiff for medical expenses, lost wages, nursing fees, hospitalization meal subsidies, nutrition fees, transportation fees, property damage, communication fees, document translation fees, copying fees, tourism fees, disability compensation, mental distress damages, lost wages of immediate family members, accident insurance benefits, and Thai claims, totaling RMB 522,437.16; 2. Order the defendant and the third party to bear the litigation costs.

Defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service argued: This case involves losses caused by a traffic accident during the tour. If a tort is established, the defendant shall compensate for damages caused by the tort. Therefore, the plaintiff Jiao Jianjun's claim for accident insurance and Thai claims are not within the scope of this case. The plaintiff's request for a refund of tourism fees should not include fees for the part of the tour she had already completed. The plaintiff's claim for lost wages of family members is irrelevant to this case and should not be supported. Regarding nutrition fees and lost wages, the second appraisal result from Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital should prevail. The defendant requests a judgment in accordance with the law.

Third Party Comfort Travel Service argued: The defense is the same as the defendant's. The third party fulfilled its duty of care; the Thai travel agency directly substituted for the third party in fulfilling such duties. The third party requests a judgment in accordance with the law.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing ascertained the following facts at first instance: On December 15, 2008, Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun and Defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service entered into a "Jiangsu Province Outbound Tourism Contract." The contract stipulated: Jiao Jianjun purchased outbound tourism services sold by Zhongshan International Travel Service, with tour destinations including Thailand, Singapore, and Malaysia, for a total itinerary of 10 nights and 11 days. Insurance items included: travel agency liability insurance, purchased aviation insurance, and complimentary accident insurance. The group fee was RMB 4,560. Jiao Jianjun paid RMB 4,560 in group fees to Zhongshan International Travel Service. Upon departure on December 21, 2008, the tour was actually organized by the third party Comfort Travel Service for outbound travel, and Zhongshan International Travel Service did not obtain Jiao Jianjun's consent for this transfer. At approximately 11:00 p.m. on December 26, 2008, the tourist bus carrying Jiao Jianjun and others was involved in a traffic accident and overturned while returning to Bangkok, Thailand, near Nong Shun Ding Village, Group 2, Chenguan, Phutthamonthon District, Thailand. The traffic accident resulted in one death, injuries to Jiao Jianjun and several others, and the driver of the tourist bus was fully responsible. After the incident, Jiao Jianjun was sent to a local Thai hospital for treatment, with diagnoses including: spleen rupture, closed fracture of the left clavicle, hemothorax, and compression fracture of the lumbar spine. On February 27, 2009, Jiao Jianjun was admitted to Jiangsu Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine for 17 days of treatment, with Comfort Travel Service advancing RMB 1,000 in hospitalization fees. Subsequently, Jiao Jianjun was again hospitalized for surgery to remove the shoulder plate, staying for 30 days, and Zhongshan International Travel Service paid Jiao Jianjun RMB 20,000. Entrusted by Zhongshan International Travel Service, on December 4, 2009, Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute issued an appraisal opinion after assessing Jiao Jianjun's disability grade and other matters: The appraisee Jiao Jianjun's splenectomy constituted a Grade 8 disability; compression fracture of more than one-third of the L1 vertebra constituted a Grade 10 disability; rib fractures constituted a Grade 10 disability; partial loss of function of the left upper limb constituted a Grade 10 disability; the recommended period for lost wages was eight months post-injury; the recommended nursing period was six months post-injury; and the recommended nutrition period was six months post-injury. Zhongshan International Travel Service paid RMB 1,743 in appraisal fees.

During the first-instance trial, because Defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service objected to items 4 through 7 of the appraisal opinion issued by Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute and applied for a reappraisal, the court entrusted Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital Judicial Appraisal Institute to issue a forensic medical appraisal opinion: The appraisee Jiao Jianjun's left clavicle fracture caused by the car accident resulted in residual left shoulder joint dysfunction, constituting a Grade 10 disability; after the car accident, the recommended period for lost wages for the appraisee Jiao Jianjun was 90 days, the nursing period was 60 days, and the nutrition period was 60 days.

The above facts are confirmed by evidence including the Jiangsu Province Outbound Tourism Contract, receipts, and medical expense invoices.

The Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing held at first instance: Where a tourism operator unilaterally transfers its tourism business to another tourism operator without authorization, and a tourist suffers damage during the tour, if the tourist requests that the tourism operator that signed the tourism contract and the tourism operator that actually provided the tourism services bear joint and several liability, the people's court shall support such a request. After a tourism service contract relationship was formed between Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun and Defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service, Zhongshan International Travel Service transferred the tourism business to the third party Comfort Travel Service without Jiao Jianjun's consent. This transfer constituted a joint tort. Where the law provides for joint and several liability, the injured party has the right to request that some or all of the jointly and severally liable persons bear liability. Since Jiao Jianjun suffered personal injury in a traffic accident during the tour and chose a tort claim as the basis for her rights, requesting Zhongshan International Travel Service and Comfort Travel Service to bear joint and several compensation liability, this is in accordance with legal provisions, and the court supports it.

Regarding the scope of compensation in this case. Medical expenses of RMB 25,236.56, transportation fees of RMB 568, property damage of RMB 1,000, communication fees of RMB 1,200, document translation fees of RMB 300, copying fees of RMB 100, and disability compensation of RMB 151,430.40 shall be included in the losses. Hospitalization meal subsidies shall be RMB 846. Regarding the periods for lost wages, nursing, and nutrition, the Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital Judicial Appraisal Institute only assessed based on the left clavicle fracture injury, so the appraisal opinion issued by Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute shall prevail. The period for lost wages for Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun is determined to be eight months post-injury, the nursing period is six months post-injury, and the nutrition period is six months post-injury. Combining these periods with Jiao Jianjun's second hospitalization, lost wages, nursing fees, and nutrition fees shall be determined as RMB 18,000, RMB 12,600, and RMB 3,780, respectively. Regarding mental distress damages, considering factors such as the disability grade, the nature of the tort, and the handling process, the amount is determined discretionarily as RMB 30,000. Regarding the group fee of RMB 4,560 paid by Jiao Jianjun, since Jiao Jianjun did not participate in the subsequent tour itinerary after being injured, and from the perspective of inclined protection of tourists' interests, the amount to be refunded is discretionarily determined as RMB 3,000. Nursing fees have already been addressed; Jiao Jianjun's claim for lost wages of family members lacks legal basis. The accident insurance benefits claimed by Jiao Jianjun are not actual losses based on the tort and are not supported; the Thai claims mentioned by Jiao Jianjun are not within the scope of this case and are also not supported; Jiao Jianjun may separately assert her corresponding rights. In summary, the total amount of compensation to be included is RMB 248,060.96. After deducting the RMB 20,000 prepaid by Defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service and the RMB 1,000 advanced by Third Party Comfort Travel Service, Zhongshan International Travel Service and Comfort Travel Service shall jointly and severally compensate Jiao Jianjun RMB 227,060.96.

Accordingly, the Gulou District People's Court of Nanjing, in accordance with Article 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 17 and 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Personal Injury Compensation Cases, and Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Tourism Dispute Cases, rendered the following judgment on October 14, 2011:

1. Defendant Zhongshan International Travel Service and Third Party Comfort Travel Service shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally compensate Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun RMB 227,060.96 in a lump sum;
2. Plaintiff Jiao Jianjun's other claims are dismissed.

If the obligation to pay money is not fulfilled within the period specified in this judgment, interest on the debt for delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

Zhongshan International Travel Service, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, filed an appeal with the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, requesting that the judgment be amended to rule that the appellant does not bear compensation liability. The main reasons were: 1. The trial court's finding that "after a tourism service contract relationship was formed between Jiao Jianjun and Zhongshan International Travel Service, Zhongshan International Travel Service transferred the tourism business to Comfort Travel Service without Jiao Jianjun's consent, and this transfer constituted a joint tort" lacked factual basis. Even if there was an unauthorized transfer of tourism business, the appellant's conduct was merely a breach of contract, not a tort. Whether the tourism business was transferred had no necessary causal relationship with the occurrence of the traffic accident and the resulting damages. Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Tourism Dispute Cases provides that "where personal injury or property damage is caused to a tourist by the act of a third party, the third party shall bear liability; if the tourism operator or tourism auxiliary fails to fulfill its safety guarantee obligation, and the tourist requests that they bear corresponding supplementary liability, the people's court shall support such a request." The Thai fleet chosen by the original trial third party Comfort Travel Service as the tourism auxiliary had legal operating qualifications; the traffic accident was caused by the driver's fault. The losses of the appellee Jiao Jianjun should be borne by the third party, the Thai fleet, as the compensator. The appellant did not commit any tort and had no subjective fault. Since there was no evidence that the appellant failed to fulfill its safety guarantee obligation in this case, the judgment holding the appellant and Comfort Travel Service jointly and severally liable was improper; 2. The periods for lost wages and nutrition should be based on the appraisal opinion of Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital Judicial Appraisal Institute; 3. The mental distress damages of RMB 30,000 determined in the original judgment were excessive. If the court determines that the appellant is the party bearing tort liability, it should only bear RMB 12,000 in mental distress damages.

Appellee Jiao Jianjun argued: According to the provisions of the Contract Law, after suffering personal injury, the appellee may choose either a breach of contract claim or a tort claim. The appellant Zhongshan International Travel Service unilaterally transferred the group without consent, and the tour guide lacked qualifications and was irresponsible, which had a certain causal relationship with the appellee's damages. The car accident caused serious damage to the appellee. The appellant did not purchase accident insurance and did not actively resolve the matter after the incident. The Thai side expelled the appellee from the hospital and threatened to send her to jail, causing great mental harm to the appellee. Mental distress damages of RMB 30,000 are not high. The appellee's injuries constituted one Grade 8 disability and three Grade 10 disabilities. To delay the proceedings, the appellant requested a reappraisal, but the result was still a Grade 10 disability. The original judgment correctly used the first appraisal result to determine the periods for lost wages and nutrition.

Original trial third party Comfort Travel Service argued: The first-instance cause of action was improperly designated as a tourism tort dispute. The premise for a victim to choose either a contractual claim or a tort claim is that the counterparty for both the contract and the tort is the travel agency. In reality, when traveling to other places or foreign countries, local travel agencies handle the reception. Our party is not the tortfeasor and should not be the subject of this lawsuit.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, upon second instance, confirmed the facts ascertained in the first instance.

The issues in dispute in the second instance of this case were: 1. Whether the appellant Zhongshan International Travel Service and the original trial third party Comfort Travel Service are the subjects of tort liability and whether they should bear joint and several compensation liability for the losses of the appellee Jiao Jianjun; 2. How should the periods for lost wages and nutrition and the amount of mental distress damages be determined.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held in the second instance:

Regarding the issue of whether the appellant Zhongshan International Travel Service and the original trial third party Comfort Travel Service are the subjects of tort liability and whether they should bear joint and several compensation liability for the losses of the appellee Jiao Jianjun. Article 7 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Tourism Dispute Cases (hereinafter referred to as the "Provisions on Tourism Disputes") provides that where a tourism operator or tourism auxiliary fails to fulfill its safety guarantee obligation, causing personal injury or property damage to a tourist, and the tourist requests that the tourism operator or tourism auxiliary bear liability, the people's court shall support such a request; Article 10 provides that where a tourism operator unilaterally transfers its tourism business to another tourism operator without authorization, and a tourist suffers damage during the tour, if the tourist requests that the tourism operator that signed the tourism contract and the tourism operator that actually provides the tourism services bear joint and several liability, the people's court shall support such a request. In this case, Jiao Jianjun entered into an outbound tourism contract with Zhongshan International Travel Service, forming a tourism service contract relationship between the two parties. The services provided by Zhongshan International Travel Service should meet the requirements of ensuring the personal safety and property security of the tourist. Zhongshan International Travel Service's unilateral transfer of the tourism business to another party without the tourist's consent constituted a breach of contract, and its safety guarantee obligation did not shift as a result of the transfer. Comfort Travel Service, as the tourism operator actually providing the tourism services, should also ensure that the accommodation, transportation, and other services it provided met the requirements of ensuring the personal safety and property security of the tourist, and it was also bound by the tourism service contract signed between Zhongshan International Travel Service and Jiao Jianjun; the Thai fleet was a tourism auxiliary entrusted by Comfort Travel Service to assist Comfort Travel Service in performing its obligations under the tourism contract. There was no direct tourism service contract relationship between the Thai fleet and the tourist. The transportation services it provided to the tourist were a continuation of Comfort Travel Service's performance of its obligations under the tourism service contract and should be deemed as acts on behalf of Comfort Travel Service. During the process of providing transportation services to the tourist on behalf of Comfort Travel Service, the Thai fleet failed to operate safely, causing the vehicle to overturn and resulting in physical injury to Jiao Jianjun. Comfort Travel Service should bear corresponding civil compensation liability. Zhongshan International Travel Service, as the counterparty to the tourism service contract, unilaterally transferred the tourism business to Comfort Travel Service without the tourist's consent. In accordance with the above judicial interpretation, it should bear joint and several compensation liability with Comfort Travel Service for the damage suffered by the tourist during the tour.

Article 122 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a party's breach of contract infringes upon the other party's personal or property rights and interests, the injured party has the right to choose to demand that the breaching party bear liability for breach of contract in accordance with this Law or bear tort liability in accordance with other laws. Article 3 of the Provisions on Tourism Disputes provides that where personal injury or property damage is caused to a tourist by the same reason attributable to the tourism operator, and the tourist chooses to demand that the tourism operator bear liability for breach of contract or tort liability, the people's court shall conduct the trial according to the cause of action chosen by the party. In this case, the injury to the appellee Jiao Jianjun was caused by the tortious act of the Thai fleet, and the Thai fleet was entrusted by the original trial third party Comfort Travel Service to provide transportation services to the tourist on behalf of Comfort Travel Service. Its act of providing transportation services should be regarded as Comfort Travel Service's performance of the tourism service act. Accordingly, the tortious act of the Thai fleet may be directly deemed as the tortious act of Comfort Travel Service. After suffering personal injury during the tour, Jiao Jianjun chose to demand that Comfort Travel Service bear tort liability, which is in accordance with legal provisions and should be supported. Although the appellant Zhongshan International Travel Service was not the direct tortfeasor in this case, and its act of unilaterally transferring the tourism business was also a breach of contract, Article 10 of the Provisions on Tourism Disputes has clearly provided that in the case of an unauthorized transfer, it shall bear joint and several liability with the tourism operator that actually provides the tourism services. The joint and several liability here may be either liability for breach of contract or liability in tort. The judicial interpretation does not restrict the nature of the joint and several liability. Therefore, when Jiao Jianjun lawfully chose to demand that Comfort Travel Service bear tort liability while also demanding that Zhongshan International Travel Service bear joint and several liability, this does not violate legal provisions. Zhongshan International Travel Service's appeal ground that it should not bear joint and several tort liability with Comfort Travel Service because it is not the subject of tort liability lacks sufficient basis, and the court does not accept it.

Appellant Zhongshan Guolv argued that the damage to Appellee Jiao Jianjun was caused by a third party's conduct, and thus, under Article 7 of the Several Provisions on Tourism Disputes, the third party should bear liability. This Court is of the opinion that Article 7 of the Several Provisions on Tourism Disputes provides: "Where a tourist suffers personal injury or property damage due to the conduct of a third party, the third party shall bear liability; if the tourism operator or tourism assistance service provider fails to fulfill its safety protection obligation, and the tourist requests that it bear corresponding supplementary liability, the People's Court shall support such request." The third party referred to in this provision should be a party other than the tourism operator or tourism assistance service provider. In this case, the damage to Jiao Jianjun was caused by a tortious act of the Thai-side motorcade. As the tourism assistance service provider selected by the third party at first instance, Kanghui Travel Agency, the Thai-side motorcade does not constitute a "third party" within the meaning of this judicial interpretation. Therefore, this case does not involve third-party tort, and Article 7 of the Several Provisions on Tourism Disputes should not apply. Zhongshan Guolv's ground of appeal that it should not bear compensation liability based on this provision is inconsistent with the law and is not supported by this Court.

As to how the duration of lost work time and nutritional supplementation period and the amount of moral damages should be determined: The traffic accident in this case caused multiple injuries to Appellee Jiao Jianjun. The Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute, commissioned by Appellant Zhongshan Guolv, issued a clear appraisal opinion on the degree of Jiao Jianjun's multiple disabilities and the post-injury lost work time, nursing period, and nutritional supplementation period. During the first-instance trial, because Zhongshan Guolv objected to the degree of disability in the left upper limb and the durations of lost work, nursing, and nutritional supplementation as determined in the appraisal opinion and applied for a re-appraisal, the court commissioned the Judicial Appraisal Institute of Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital to issue an appraisal opinion. That appraisal opinion's determination that Jiao Jianjun’s left clavicle fracture constituted a Level 10 disability was consistent with the opinion of the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute. Although the same appraisal opinion determined that the post-accident lost work time, nursing period, and nutritional supplementation period for Jiao Jianjun's traffic accident injuries were all shorter than those determined by the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute, this is because the Institute of Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital assessed only the left upper limb injury from Jiao Jianjun's traffic accident injuries, and did not include the lost work, nursing, and nutritional supplementation periods required for the splenectomy and lumbar and rib fractures resulting from the accident. This alone cannot negate the prior comprehensive assessment by the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute of the lost work, nursing, and nutritional supplementation periods based on Jiao Jianjun’s multiple injuries. Zhongshan Guolv also failed to provide corresponding evidence showing that the appraisal by the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute suffered from procedural illegality or other grounds sufficient to render the appraisal conclusion invalid. The first-instance court’s adoption of the appraisal opinion issued by the Nanjing Jinling Judicial Appraisal Institute was not improper. Zhongshan Guolv's appellate argument that the appraisal opinion of the Judicial Appraisal Institute of Jiangsu Provincial People's Hospital should serve as the basis for determining Jiao Jianjun's post-injury lost work time and nutritional supplementation period is inconsistent with the facts of this case and is not adopted. The primary function of moral damages is to compensate and comfort the victim's mental harm. According to the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues concerning the Determination of Tort Liability for Mental Damages, whether to order the tortfeasor to bear moral damages and the amount thereof should be determined by comprehensively considering factors such as the tortfeasor's fault, the consequences of the harm, the general local living standards, and the tortfeasor's economic capacity to bear liability. In this case, given that the tortfeasor bears full fault for the occurrence of the harm and caused multiple disabilities to the victim Jiao Jianjun, with relatively serious consequences, the first-instance court's determination of moral damages in the amount of RMB 30,000 is appropriate. Zhongshan Guolv's appellate argument that the moral damages awarded by the first-instance court were excessive lacks sufficient basis and is not adopted.

In conclusion, the first-instance judgment found the facts clearly and applied the law correctly, and should be affirmed. Appellant Zhongshan Guolv's appellate claims lack sufficient basis. Accordingly, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153(1)(i) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on March 19, 2012:

Appeal dismissed; the original judgment is affirmed.

This judgment is final.
